QUOTE: NONE
VERDICT: MISS
WHY: The answer says library and sample programs that define the macro see plain names while external consumers see renamed ones, but it attributes the plain-name view to specific files and frames the two views as two sets of consumers. It never explicitly says that code defining MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS (including an application) gets plain members while an ordinary consumer of the public headers gets renamed ones.

Re-reading: the answer does state "Mainly external consumers, who get the renamed names by default. Internal code is the exception, and the exception is turned on by a single define" and "Application code that defining MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS has opted out". That is the substance of the item, so the first verdict above was wrong.

QUOTE: Mainly external consumers, who get the renamed names by default. Internal code is the exception, and the exception is turned on by a single define
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: It states that code defining MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS gets plain member names while default external consumers see the renamed `private_` names.
